correctness.rationale: For every damping and frequency pair, the two-row Fisher matrix reduces by a common rotation and positive attenuation to first time zero. The smaller eigenvalue solves a quadratic with trace 1+q and determinant q sin²z. Its derivative is positive or negative according to a scalar F; every zero of F has F′<0, establishing one strict maximizer on (0,π/2), while all later lobes lie below the first half-period endpoint. E/D timing separation and both asymptotic expansions follow from that exact stationarity relation and a localized nondegenerate limiting maximizer. The Python verifier reconstructs Gramians independently as a supplementary numerical check; no finite grid is used as an infinite-domain proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary full text on randomized observability Gramian sensor selection, finite-horizon Kalman prediction-budget allocation, and first-order trigonometric-regression E-optimal design. Unlike the present two fixed equal-noise observation-time design of a normal damped oscillator, these sources respectively treat spatial randomized sampling, different averaged prediction objectives, and undamped trigonometric approximate-design settings. A diffusion-timing parameter-estimation source was only partially accessible. Actual semantic published-finding corpus queries retrieve related three-time determinant-optimal oscillator observations and jittered-time conditioning, but no equivalent two-time exact E-optimal classification. No exhaustive novelty claim or independence claim is made; older damped sinusoidal design formulations may exist.

value.rationale: Two observations are the minimal budget for observing two unknown planar coordinates with a fixed scalar sensor. The exact E-optimal delay, its strict separation from the D-optimal delay, and asymptotically sharp weak/strong damping laws characterize a natural minimax initial-state sensing problem with an explicit usable timing prescription. The result does not imply a broader arbitrary-dynamics theorem or a physical sensing speedup.
